name: Pločnik tin-bronze foil
summary: A tin-bronze foil found in a Pločnik house, made by about 4650 BCE, appears to come from smelting naturally mixed copper-tin ores, then hammering and annealing.
description: Tin-bronze foil interpreted as metal smelted from complex copper–tin ores, subsequently worked and annealed.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: One foil showing an early alloy that was apparently not passed on; scores imply tier 3, well below the reviewed tier 1.

links.statement: Did knowledge of copper smelting at Belovode reach the makers of the Pločnik tin-bronze foil, sample 63?
links.caveats: The sites share a Vinča setting. The carriers, route and direction of any knowledge transfer remain unresolved.
links.finding: The 2013 analysis infers complex copper–tin ore for foil sample 63. The 2021 comparisons concern separate ordinary-copper finds. The sources leave open how the foil's makers acquired their smelting knowledge.

evidence.locator: p. 1032, find context; pp. 1035–1039, sample 63 analysis
evidence.supports: Sample 63 is the worked tin-bronze foil. The authors infer a complex copper–tin ore.

evidence.locator: Table 3, Group 3 and Fig. 7; Fig. 15, trace-element comparison
evidence.supports: The geochemical comparisons concern the ordinary-copper ring C_P2/13, chisel HDM1586 and foil P10/13. The comparisons give no evidence that Belovode smelting knowledge reached the makers of sample 63.
